title: When You’re Feeling Impatient
summary: Notice impatience and practice waiting calmly: your turn, to wait your turn.
script:
Hi. Welcome. Welcome to this meditation while you learn English.
Wherever you're sitting or lying down right now, let yourself be calm, exactly as you are. No rushing to get comfortable, just arrive slowly.
Close your eyes, or let your eyes soften.
Nothing to hurry through here. Just a few quiet minutes. Okay?
Inhale slowly.
And exhale, letting your shoulders drop a little as you do.
One more time. Inhale… and exhale.
I want you to think of a moment recently when you had to wait for something. Maybe a line somewhere. Maybe a message that hadn't come yet. Maybe just a moment where someone else was speaking,and you had to wait for them to finish so that you could say something.
Bring that feeling gently into your mind.
Notice what happens in your body when waiting feels hard. Sometimes your leg starts moving. Maybe your breath gets a little shorter. Maybe your mind starts thinking about what will happen next instead of focusing on the present
Inhale slowly.
This feeling of always wanting things to happen faster is called impatience. You want to move ahead instead of waiting. Often, it comes from feeling like it should already be your turn.
“Your turn” simply means the moment when it’s time for you to do something. Before your turn, other people or things may need to go first. Think of a line at a supermarket checkout counter: everyone waits until it's their turn.
Exhale slowly.
Notice, honestly, if there is a part of you right now that feels like it's been waiting a little too long for its turn. Maybe about something small today. Maybe about something much bigger in your life.
Inhale again.
Here's something worth noticing about lines like that. Everyone standing in them wants their turn just as much as you want yours. Nobody's turn actually skips ahead just because someone wants it badly enough. The line moves the way it moves, one person, one moment, at a time.
Exhale slowly.
There is a skill in learning to wait your turn. It means letting things happen in the right order without rushing or forcing them. You trust that your moment will come, even when it’s someone else’s turn right now.
Let's practice this, gently, right now.
Inhale slowly.
Imagine you’re standing in that same line. Instead of feeling restless or trying to move ahead, simply stand calmly where you are. Your turn has not disappeared. It just hasn't come yet.
Exhale, and let your shoulders drop with that same realization: not yet doesn't mean never.
Not yet doesn't mean never.
Notice your breath now, and let it move at its own natural rhythm, without rushing it either. Even your breathing has its own turn, taking in air, and then, patiently, letting it go, one at a time, never trying to inhale and exhale simultaneously, never rushing that natural order.
So now inhale again, noticing this rhythm.
And exhale, noticing how naturally it happens, without force.
This is what it means to wait your turn. You don't feel angry or tense. You simply slow down and trust that your time will come, just like your breath comes naturally, not too early and not too late.
Let 's inhale again.
Bring to mind again whatever you're currently waiting for, whatever moment still feels a little out of reach right now. Instead of pushing against it, try simply saying, quietly, "My turn is coming."
"My turn is coming."
Notice how that feels, even if it feels slightly unfamiliar. That's alright. Waiting patiently is a practice, not something that happens perfectly right away.
Now let’s exhale completely.
You don't need to enjoy waiting. You just need to trust, a little more, that waiting your turn doesn't mean being forgotten, it simply means the line is moving the way it's supposed to, and your moment is still somewhere ahead of you, closer now than it was a few minutes ago. You can wait your turn.
And if you’d like, you can repeat a few words after me.
My turn is coming, even if it hasn't arrived yet.
My turn is coming, even if it hasn't arrived yet.
I don't have to push for something that's already on its way.
I don't have to push for something that's already on its way.
Waiting doesn't mean I've been forgotten.
Waiting doesn't mean I've been forgotten.
I trust the timing of my own life, even the waiting parts.
I trust the timing of my own life, even the waiting parts.
Take one more slow inhale.
And exhale, completely.
Feeling a little bit more patient, than when you begin.
When you're ready to come back, start noticing small, real things around you. Whatever is supporting your body right now. Any sound nearby. Your breath. Your fingers. Then your feet.
And whenever it feels right, let your eyes open.
Carry this with you, into whatever waiting comes next in your day. Impatience may still visit sometimes, that's alright, it's simply energy without anywhere to go yet. But you know, a little more clearly, how it feels to wait your turn, calmly, and unhurried, trusting that your moment is still coming.

vocabulary.definition: the feeling of always wanting things to happen faster
the moment when it’s time for you to do something
to let things happen in the right order without rushing or forcing them
